title: TraceMap
description: Where every character of one artefact came from. musubi is the reference producer, not required to be the only one. THIS SCHEMA DESCRIBES SHAPE ONLY: the invariant the map exists for -- that the segments cover every character of the artefact exactly once -- is not expressible in JSON Schema. See docs/contracts.md, section 'What these schemas cannot say'.

contract.description: A consumer that does not recognise this value refuses the map rather than guessing at it (ADR-0002). The -draft suffix is a state of the contract register, not a property of this document: a draft and a frozen map of the same contract have the same shape, because freezing constrains what future versions may do. Whether the freeze has happened, and on what condition, is in docs/contracts.md, which can be corrected; a schema saying so would go on saying it after the freeze.

artefact.description: The document this map is about, as musubi wrote it.

path.description: Relative to the destination, and derived from the unit_key rather than from the source's filename (ADR-0013).

source.description: What the artefact was made from, and what it takes to read an offset in it.

unit_key.description: Stable across exports of the same data (ADR-0006), NFC, '/'-joined (ADR-0014).

encoding.description: How the source was decoded. With this, bom_bytes and the file, a character offset becomes a byte offset (ADR-0018). Without the file, nothing can.

bom_bytes.description: Bytes a byte-order mark consumed. Three on a file a Windows producer wrote without being asked, and a real offset difference.

converter.description: Which implementation built the artefact: markdown@1, pdf_text@1.

source_unit.description: What a source offset indexes, and a reader must branch on it before doing arithmetic: [0:1] is one character or one page and the two look identical. 'characters' is characters of the decoded source (ADR-0018), and a byte offset can be derived from it with the encoding and the file. 'opaque' is a locator with no decoded text behind it -- a PDF page (ADR-0025) -- and no byte offset can be derived from it at all. A reader that does not recognise the value refuses the map rather than reading page indices as character offsets.

coverage.description: The numerator and the denominator, published together so that a reader aggregating over a corpus uses the right total rather than averaging ratios.

traceable.description: Characters in a verbatim or transformed segment. NOT CHECKED HERE: that this is at most `characters`, or that it equals the sum of the traceable segments' lengths.

segments.description: Ordered by output offset. Source ranges need NOT be monotonic: a two-column page read in reading order produces a map whose source ranges jump, and the jump is information rather than a defect. NOT CHECKED HERE: the ordering, or that the segments tile the artefact.

hash.description: Names its own algorithm, so a future change is a data change an old reader can refuse rather than a silent reinterpretation (ADR-0015).

span.description: A half-open range, [start, end). NOT CHECKED HERE: that end is at least start. JSON Schema 2020-12 cannot compare two members of the same array.

segment.description: One run of the artefact, and the run of the source it accounts for.

kind.description: verbatim: the source's own characters. transformed: the same content in different characters; the correspondence holds at the ends and nowhere inside. synthetic: musubi wrote it, and src is where it was put rather than where it came from. removal: something was taken out; occupies no output and a real stretch of source (ADR-0005).

rule.description: Why this is not verbatim: a cleansing rule id, a converter's reason, the name of what musubi inserted.

allOf.description: A verbatim run names no rule: nothing happened to it, so there is nothing to attribute.
